title: Alekhine Defense: Modern Variation
line: White develops calmly; Black trades the center pawn and steps around a famous knight sacrifice.

steps.text: In the Modern Variation, White guards the pawn on e5 with a knight instead of more pawns.

also.c8g4: That pins the knight, and it is also played. This lesson takes the pawn.
also.g7g6: That is also played. This lesson takes the pawn first.

steps.text: A famous trap: if your other knight comes to d7, White gives a knight on f7 and drags your king into the open.
So push the pawn on g7 one square instead, to bring your bishop out.

wrong.b8d7: That is the trap: White's knight takes on f7 and your king is dragged into the open.

also.c7c6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the bishop.
also.e7e6: That also works. This lesson goes on with the bishop.

steps.text: Push the pawn on c7 one square. It guards your knight on d5.
Castle. Your king goes to safety, and a rook comes toward the center.
steps.after: Your king is safe, the knight never went to d7, and the bishop on g7 aims at White's knight on e5.

summary: In the Modern, Black takes the center pawn and keeps the knight off the square that walks into the sacrifice.
